texts: My colleague just got his third raise this year and is already furious that his friend got a bigger one, like a fish that bites at every hook it sees.
The fish leaps at the glittering bait, hungering for more, and never sees the hook until it is too late.
fish, hunger for more
doha about a fish chasing bait, how greed never stops
Write a doha about a fish that swallows bait after bait without ever feeling full, to show how hunger for more gain drives a person on without end, however much he already has.
The more desire is given, the more it demands; wanting is a hunger that grows by being fed.
He got the promotion, the car and the bigger place, and by next month he was already scanning listings for something better.
doha about how wanting more never ends
never enough
Please write a doha about the craving that grows with every success, so that the one who earns a lakh wants ten, the one with ten wants a crore, and none of it ever feels like enough.
heron, endless hunger
Watching a heron stand in the shallows for hours, I thought about my cousin, who is never done hunting for the next deal, even when he is rich.
A heron stands patiently waiting for the next catch though its belly is already full, just as a man hunts for more profit long after he has plenty. Please write a doha about this endless hunger.
The heron stands and stares at the water, full yet hungry, for desire has no belly that can be filled.
doha with a heron, about people who always want more profit
I sold the family business for a good price and was happy for one week; then I started worrying that I should have asked for more, and I still do.
A drop of dew is never enough for the thirst of desire, which takes in the whole world and still cries for more.
doha with dew in it, about wanting more and more and never being satisfied
Please write a doha where a single drop of dew is offered to a hungry heart that swallows it and demands another, showing that craving cannot be filled however much it receives.
dew, thirst unquenched
My uncle keeps buying lottery tickets, more each week, like a blind man hoping the next one will light everything up, and he never stops to count what he has lost.
A blind man gropes along the cloth sheet spread with goods, grabbing at everything within reach, never knowing what he already holds. Please write a doha on how blind craving grabs for more and more.
doha with a cloth sheet and a blind man, about greedy grabbing
The blind man gropes across the cloth sheet, gathering everything and holding nothing, for craving has no eyes.
blind man, cloth sheet, grabbing
In the forest of desire, the traveller plunges deeper, chasing mirages across the sand, thirstier with every step.
doha about a forest and sand, how chasing more never ends
My brother keeps investing in the next big scheme, deeper and deeper in, like someone lost in a forest running on sand, certain the next clearing will be it.
Write a doha where a person wanders through a forest and across the sand, always certain the next stretch holds the prize he wants, and every step only deepens his thirst for more.
forest, sand, endless thirst
lamp, hunger for more
The lamp burns bright yet asks for more oil, as desire asks for more of everything and is never full.
doha with a lamp, about wanting more more more
Please write a doha about a lamp that must be fed again and again, burning bright and demanding fuel, to show how craving for gain devours whatever it is given and always asks for more.
I fill up my wish list every month, and the things I buy light me up for a day, but by evening, I'm wanting the next thing again.
My friend's parrot repeats the word more, more, and I swear it describes his master, who sifts through every deal like a winnowing fan hunting for a bigger profit.
doha with a parrot and a winnowing fan, how people always want more profit
Write a doha where a parrot keeps repeating its demand for more while a man with a winnowing fan sifts for just a little more gain, to show how craving feeds on itself and never stops.
parrot, winnowing fan, more
The parrot cries for more, the winnowing fan sifts for more, and the heart that follows both is never full.
hunger for more gain
Wanting grows by being satisfied, taking whatever it is given and asking again.
write a doha about greedy desire that is never satisfied
Please compose a doha about the man whose profits double each year and who is more anxious and hungry with each doubling, because craving for gain is a thirst that more drink can only increase.
She makes more than she ever dreamed, and still every night she checks her colleague's salary and calls herself poor.
The mirror shows a hungry face that wants more, and no gain in the world can fill the face it sees.
mirror, never satisfied
A man stands before a mirror and sees only what he lacks, never what he has, and the more he gains, the more the face in the mirror frowns. Write a doha on this restless craving.
Every morning my neighbour checks his reflection in the mirror and then his stock prices, and he always looks like he is missing something.
doha with a mirror in it, about always wanting more than you have
The traveller stays at the inn but dreams of the next, hungering for a better room, and so the road has no end.
doha with an inn, about always wanting something better
Write a doha about a man who stays at one inn after another, forever convinced the next will be better, and who cannot enjoy any of them because his craving always looks ahead for more.
We moved flats four times in five years, each time because the next one was supposed to be better, and I realise now it is me that I haven't moved past.
inn, restless wanting
doha about a thorn and a market, how craving for profit hurts us
Every day my aunt haggles in the market for a few more rupees off and comes back with scratches of worry like thorns in her mind; I want a doha on that.
In the market of desire, the thorn pricks the hand that grabs, yet the hand grabs again.
thorn, market, craving
Please compose a doha about a trader in the market whose hands bleed from the thorns of his own greed, yet who keeps reaching for more profit, because desire does not feel its own wounds.
A king keeps adding wings to his palace and a traveller stands at the crossroads, unsure which road leads to more; please write a doha on how the hunger for more never lets anyone rest.
doha with a palace and a crossroads, about never being satisfied
The palace grows another tower and the road splits at the crossroads, and still the hungry heart says, not yet.
palace, crossroads, wanting more
At the crossroads near our old palace ruin I thought of a relative who keeps expanding his big place and still says, it is not enough.
doha about a thread and scales, how greed makes people cheat for more profit
The scales tilt by a hair, the thread is spun a little thin, and the heart that hungers calls it a clever gain.
Write a doha about a trader who tips the scales just a little and pulls the thread a little thin to gain a bit more, showing how hunger for profit leads a man to a never-ending trickery.
Our local grocer has been caught adjusting his scales and cutting the thread of his long-standing customers' trust, all for a few extra rupees.
thread, scales, cheating hunger
The net is cast wider and wider, and the hunger of desire still cries for more.
My brother keeps adding businesses like someone casting a net wider each day, and he never sits down to enjoy what has come in.
doha with a net, about wanting more and more catch
net, hungry for more
Please write a doha about a net cast wider after every haul, as a man who has caught plenty still hungers for more, to show how desire is a thirst that no catch can quench.
one-string lute, stone
The one-string lute sings of desire's endless song, but the stone in its heart never softens.
Write a doha about the one-string lute that plays a single tune of wanting, while the listener, hard as stone, only asks for a longer song and a bigger reward, never satisfied by what he hears.
doha with a one-string lute and a stone, about being greedy and never full
A street singer plays his one-string lute for hours, and the stone-faced man who listens says, one more, one more, never giving enough to even buy him tea.
doha about people who always want more and are never satisfied
Please write a doha about the way a hunger for gain grows even larger when fed, so that the more a man gets, the poorer he feels, because his craving is a hole that cannot be filled.
insatiable hunger
My cousin won a big prize and the next week he was complaining that it wasn't big enough.
Give desire the whole world and it will still ask, is that all?
My roommate cannot enjoy any meal because he is already planning his next order, and the next, and yet always wants one more dish.
doha about craving more and more food, money, everything
always wanting more
O hungry heart, you take the whole world in and cry for more, as though it were nothing.

Please compose a doha for a person who has everything and is still checking what others have, whose appetite for more gain has become so loud that it drowns out any chance of enjoying what is already his.
The bee flits from flower to flower, sipping more and more, and never sips enough, for the hunger is not in the flower but in the bee.
I watched a bee circle the same garden for an hour as if the nectar from each bloom was never quite right, and I thought of my own search for the perfect deal.

Write a doha about the bee that moves from bloom to bloom without ever settling, always sure that the next will be sweeter, to show that craving for more is a restlessness that can never be satisfied.
bee, restless hunger
doha with a bee, about people who always want more
doha with a house in it, about wanting a bigger and bigger place
Every time my brother upgrades his house he is happy for a month, and then starts browsing for a bigger one; I'd like a doha on him.
house, bigger and bigger
A small house became a big one, the big one a mansion, and the mansion a longing for another.
Please write a doha about a man who builds a larger house each time he earns more, never satisfied with the rooms he has, and who finds that desire grows as fast as the walls.
My sister earns more than all of us, yet she keeps asking for a raise and a bigger bonus each year, as if the number could one day make her feel safe.
gain without end
Please write a doha about a person who gets the thing he wanted and instantly wants the next thing, so that his desire, satisfied for a moment, rises again like hunger after a meal.
Desire receives everything and calls it a taste.
need a doha on how greed makes us want more than we need
I want a doha about the endless race for more, more followers, more money, more praise, and how each win only makes us more hungry, so that the finish line of enough keeps moving farther away.
wanting never ends
My friend posted a photo, got a thousand likes, and was upset that it wasn't two thousand; I wonder what Kabir would say.
pls write a doha about greed for more and more
What the hungry heart receives, it forgets at once and craves again; such is the way of desire.
My uncle looked into his bathroom mirror and said, I look rich now, and then went out to chase the next deal that would make him richer.
doha with a mirror, about greed and wanting more than you need
Write a doha where a man looks into a mirror and sees all that he has gained, but his face is only hungry, for in the mirror of craving no amount of gain is ever enough.
mirror, hungry for more
Before the mirror stands desire, looking for the next prize, and the mirror shows a face that has never been satisfied.
doha with a bier, about how greed doesnt stop even at the end
Even beside the bier, the greedy hand reaches for one thing more, for craving does not know when to rest.
bier, craving to the end
At my uncle's last rites, some relatives were already asking whose share would be bigger, even as the bier was being prepared.
Please write a doha about the person whose craving for gain is so strong it follows him to the foot of the bier, where he still thinks of what he wishes he had and cannot let go of wanting.
My friend always wants a bigger car, like an elephant that eats and eats and still seeks more, and then he stares at the sky like a chakor bird waiting for something it can never reach.
An elephant eats its fill and still looks for more, and a chakor bird gazes endlessly at a thing it can never have; please write a doha showing how the craving for more can never be filled.
elephant, chakor bird, craving
The elephant swallows a thousand mouthfuls and still hungers, the chakor bird stares at a prize it cannot reach, and desire is both.
doha with an elephant and a chakor bird, about greed that never ends
The tenant in the next lane built a second floor for his house and now says he needs a third, as if there were no limit, and I wish someone would write him a doha.

Please write a doha about a man who owns a house and is not satisfied until he owns the neighbouring plot too, and then the next, because the craving for more gain never lets him enjoy the house he has.
A house is built, a house is bought, and the heart still roams the streets looking for another.
doha with a house, about someone always wanting more property
house, endless wanting
doha about greedy people who just keep wanting
hunger that grows
The more he gains, the less he has, for the heart that hungers grows poorer with every prize.
She was thrilled with the first customer, then the tenth, then the hundredth, and now she is miserable because she doesn't have a thousand.
Please compose a doha about the way a hunger for profit can eat a person from within, so that even as his income rises he feels poorer each day because the number he is chasing keeps moving away.
The wanting is never full, however much gain comes into it.
doha for me about how greedy desire is never satisfied
Please write a doha about the way a person's craving expands to fit whatever he gains, so that every victory only widens the appetite and leaves him feeling just as empty as before.
desire, never full
When my brother got his bonus he was thrilled for a day, and then he said, imagine if it were double.
Last summer my father kept pushing his orchard to produce more fruit each year, like a man shaking a tree that has nothing left, until the tree itself gave up.
Write a doha about a man who shakes a tree for a few more fruits long after the branches are bare, to show that hunger for gain keeps taking even when there is nothing left to take.
tree, shaken for more
Shake the tree again, says desire, though the branches are bare, and the tree gives up its leaves and still hears, more.
doha with a tree in it, about taking and taking until nothing is left
Gold is piled before a man and he picks up a stone to hammer at it, hoping to make it more, and I'd like a doha showing that craving is never satisfied by gold, however much he is handed.
doha with a stone and gold, about greedy people wanting even more
gold, stone, never enough
Give the greedy heart a heap of gold and it will crack a stone, hoping to find more inside.
My uncle's jeweller hands him gold bangles worth lakhs, and he still turns each one over like a stone he hopes will hide something more.
A man in a big house looks over to the neighbour's palace and cannot sleep, convinced that his own home is not enough; please write a doha on how craving makes us restless however much we have.
Our house is big and comfortable, but my husband still goes to see the palace-like villa down the road every weekend, as if it held something he was missing.
doha with a house and a palace, about always wanting something bigger
The house looks across at the palace, and the palace looks beyond, and the hungry heart is nowhere at home.
house, palace, envy and wanting
Please write a doha about the way a person who gets everything he asked for in life still sits awake wanting the next thing, because craving is a hunger that grows each time it is satisfied.
At my cousin's wedding the groom was already talking about his next business, and I wondered if he had even noticed the day.
wanting more, always
The hungry heart takes in every pleasure and, rising, asks what else the world can offer.
doha about being greedy and never full pls
My neighbour has three businesses and works through the night for a fourth, and when I asked him why, he said, just a little more.
greedy and never full
Little by little more, he says, until the little has consumed the whole of life.
doha about the never ending hunger for more profit
Please write a doha for someone whose income has doubled twice but whose happiness has not, who wishes to understand how craving always sets the finish line just beyond where he stands.
doha with stars and a river, about wanting everything and never getting enough
The river of desire runs toward the stars and still runs dry, for it drinks the sky and cries for more.
Write a doha where a man tries to reach the stars by following a river that never ends, and with every step the stars seem to retreat, to show how craving moves out of reach as it is pursued.
Late at night by the river I look at the stars and think of how much I want and how none of what I get is ever enough.
stars, river, endless longing
endless hunger for gain
Every deal I close feels great for exactly one hour, and then I check what my rival has closed, and the whole cycle begins again.
Run, run, runs the hungry heart, after the prize that retreats with every step.
Please compose a doha about greed that feeds on its own satisfaction, making a man hungrier the more he receives, until his whole life becomes a chase after something he will never feel is enough.
write a doha about wanting more and more and never enough
potter and clay, shadow
doha with a potter and clay and a shadow, about greedy desire never ending
The potter shapes the clay yet cannot shape his wanting, and his shadow grows longer as he reaches for more.
The potter in our colony makes a hundred pots a day and still takes extra orders until his shadow stretches across the lane at dusk, never satisfied with what he has made.
Write a doha about a potter who works clay all day for profit, and as his earnings grow his shadow of wanting grows too, longer and longer, so that he can never rest in what he has.
net, musk deer, craving

A musk deer runs through the undergrowth searching for the scent it carries itself, and a man casts his net for more, never seeing that the hunger lies within him; write a doha on this restless craving.
My boss hunts after new clients like a musk deer that sniffs everywhere for a scent it carries itself, and keeps casting his net wider though his quarter was the best ever.
doha with a net and a musk deer, about greed that looks everywhere but inside
The musk deer runs and the net is cast, yet the thing that is hungered for lives in the hunger itself.

Please write a doha about the endless wanting that spoils each pleasure before it is enjoyed, so that a man who gets what he asked for already begins hunting for what comes next, and never lives in the present.
Desire has no bottom; give it all a king owns and it still cries for a little more.
doha pls about wanting more and more profit
When I finally got the corner office I looked around for about ten seconds and then wondered how soon I could get the one with the view.
bottomless wanting
bier, fly, craving
At the cremation, a fly kept circling the sweets laid out for guests, and the relatives were already arguing about the bier expenses and who would get more; I'd like a doha on it.
doha with a bier and a fly, about greed that doesnt even stop for death
Write a doha where a fly buzzes around the sweet as people crowd near the bier, still grabbing at what they can, to show that the hunger for gain is so persistent that even grief cannot stop it.
The fly hovers at the bier for one more crumb, and the heart hovers at the world for one more gain.
doha with a market and a parrot, how greed makes people always want more
Every Saturday my mother-in-law drags us to the market, buys things she doesn't need, and her pet parrot keeps shouting for more food, just like her.
In the market the parrot repeats, buy, buy, buy, and the heart that hungers hears no other word.
market, parrot, wanting more
Write a doha where a parrot trained to say more sits in a market full of goods, and the shoppers around it, hungry for gains and bargains, answer its cry without ever having enough.
My roommate cannot watch a movie without also scrolling for deals, and no deal is enough; the cycle runs all day and I think a doha would help him see it.
Craving widens as it is fed, and never reaches its own end.
write a doha for a friend who wants more more more
hunger, never fed
Please write a doha about the strange poverty of the person who has everything, but whose mind is always on what he does not have, and who therefore spends each day in a state of lack.
Desire says, one more, and when the one is given, it says, one more, until a life is lost in the counting.
My neighbour added another side business last year and another this year, and now he sleeps four hours a night, telling everyone it is almost enough.
doha on how greed keeps growing, never full
one more, always
Write a doha for those who tell themselves that after this next gain they will rest, but find that craving always raises the bar, so that their rest never comes and their hunger only grows.
At the door of every meeting my boss tells us that the target next quarter must be double, and no number is ever enough, and I can see the scales never balancing in his mind.
The door of desire is always open, the scales never balanced, and the hungry heart walks in and out forever.
doha with a door and scales, about greed that never balances

Write a doha where a man stands at a door with a pair of scales, always weighing what he has against what others have, and finding that his craving makes the scale tilt toward lack no matter what he adds.
door, scales, never enough
wanting without end
The moment I paid off my loan I started looking at a bigger one for a bigger flat, which is apparently how people like me are made.
doha for someone who is never happy with their gains
Hungry heart, what is it you seek? Every prize you win becomes only the beginning of the next.
Please compose a doha that tells how a craving mind turns each victory into a starting line, so that no matter how far a person travels in profit, his desire only stretches the road further ahead.
priest, greed for more
The priest recites of renunciation while his eyes count the offerings, and craving robes itself in holy words.
Please write a doha about a priest who preaches letting go but quietly measures every donation and wants more of it, showing that hunger for gain can hide even in the one who preaches against it.
Our priest is always saying that wanting is the root of suffering, then looks disappointed when the donation box is lighter than last month.
doha about a priest who preaches but is greedy for offerings
parrot, repeated wanting
doha with a parrot, about greedy people repeating I want more
Write a doha about a parrot that has learned just one phrase, I want more, and repeats it day and night at every feeding, to show the human hunger for gain that cannot be quieted by getting.
The parrot cries for more with the voice of man, or man with the voice of the parrot; neither is ever satisfied.
My uncle's parrot has learned to say one more, one more, from hearing my uncle bargain with everyone for years.
always hungry for more
At the buffet my cousin piled his plate high, went back twice, and then complained he hadn't tried everything, while his stomach was already full.
doha on how greedy people keep taking more than they need
Please compose a doha about a man who is given a handful and asks for a basketful, and is given a basketful and asks for a field, for the hunger of craving only grows with what it is given.
Give him a little and he asks for a lot; give him a lot and he asks for everything.
Gain after gain the hungry heart devours, and the ledger shows more, yet the soul shows less.
Please write a doha for the man who counts his income each evening and feels cheated that it is not more, whose craving has turned his best days into a long, unsatisfied accounting.
doha about wanting more profit all the time
gain, never enough
My father's business earns twice what it used to, but he sits grumbling over the ledger as if we were ruined.

Write a doha about the bee that visits a thousand flowers and still circles for more, as a picture of the human hunger for gain that never says that is enough, and forever searches the next sweet thing.
The bee sips from a thousand flowers and still goes buzzing, for the hunger of the sipper is deeper than any flower.
At the orchard I noticed a single bee moving restlessly from bloom to bloom without ever staying, and it reminded me of how my brother treats every opportunity.
doha with a bee, about people who always want more gain
bee, never satisfied
greed, never full
Give desire the whole world's abundance and it will ask for the next season's too.
My grandmother says that when she was young a single sweet at festival time was happiness, and now my kids get gifts all year and always want the next thing.
Please write a doha about the way wanting more is passed from one generation to the next, so that each new thing, however bright, becomes boring by evening and the hunger for another takes its place.
write a doha on how greed keeps growing the more you get
